newsitem.title: USA: Footstar stocks slump after outlook.
newsitem.headline: Footstar stocks slump after outlook.

text.p: Footstar Inc.'s stock shed more than 25 percent of its value after the athletic footwear retailer reported better-than-expected first-quarter profits but said it sees signs of slowing in recent sales in its sector.
The stock fell $6.50 in heavy trading to $18.625, topping the percentage losers on the New York Stock Exchange.

Footstar, which operates Footaction and Meldisco athletic footwear stores, posted earnings per share of $5 million, or 16 cents per share, compared with $900,000, or 3 cents a share. According to First Call, Wall Street analysts expected earnings of 9 cents a share.

But in the earnings release, Footstar Chairman and Chief Executive Mickey Robinson said that on the heels of a strong 1996, "recent sales trends and the athletic sector in general have shown signs of slowing.

"However, we have planned conservatively and expect Footstar to deliver bottom-line results for the year as anticipated through effective cost control and inventory management," the statement continued.
Footstar is based in Mahwah, N.J.
